title: For 0<q<1, theta>0 and any integer signature, the one-variable Macdonald character has the absolutely convergent q-Gamma contour formula of Theorem 3.2 for nonzero x of absolute value at most one
author: Cesar Cuenca
work: Asymptotic Formulas for Macdonald Polynomials and the Boundary of the (q,t)-Gelfand-Tsetlin Graph
source_version: Official SIGMA 14 (2018) article 001, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2018.001; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The identity for an arbitrary positive real deformation parameter requires substantially more than taking residues at finitely many integer poles. The author first constructs a discrete-parameter contour formula and then proves the uniform estimates needed for holomorphic continuation and Carlson uniqueness on an unbounded parameter half-plane. Infinite-contour convergence, general integer signatures and the unit-circle boundary are all treated in the supplied proof.

source_check.note: The complete original Theorem 3.2 and detailed Steps 0–4 are retained for all real theta>0, integer signatures and nonzero |x|<=1. The full new integer-parameter Theorem 3.1 proof is bundled as uncounted core, including index shifts, deformation/interpolation and finite-pole control. Complete new q-Gamma tail estimates, compact-uniform holomorphy/Morera and unbounded right-half-plane Carlson bounds, boundary domination and signature shifts are supplied. Macdonald symmetry/evaluation/branching, q-binomial identities and Carlson uniqueness remain author-cited standard prerequisites. The exact C-plus contour and logarithm convention are retained. The neighboring Theorem 3.3 has explicitly omitted details and is not counted; neither multiplicative formulas nor Martin-boundary results are selected. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: Complete Theorem3.2 proof Sections3.3-3.5 was read, including the integer-theta support theorem3.1. The author obtains the integer case from index-argument symmetry and one-row generating functions, deforms the contour and interpolates in x. For all positive real theta he supplies absolute q-Gamma tail estimates, complex-theta holomorphy via compact-uniform domination and Morera, uniform right-half-plane boundedness for Carlson uniqueness, signature shifts and boundary dominated convergence. Theorem3.3 details are explicitly omitted by the source and are not selected. Macdonald evaluation/branching and Carlson uniqueness are established cited background.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem3.2: real q in (0,1), real theta>0, t=q^theta, positive integer N, integer nonincreasing signature lambda in GT_N and complex x nonzero with absolute value <=1. Retain the normalized ratio P_lambda(x*t^(N-1),t^(N-2),...,1)/P_lambda(t^(N-1),...,1), exact q-Gamma prefactor, and the positively oriented C-plus contour with lambda_N>M and 0<r<-pi/(2*ln(q)). Retain the logarithm convention of Remark3.4. No independent multiplicative formula, boundary classification or omitted Theorem3.3 is counted.
